hypotheses.claim: Global addressability is weaker than causal broadcast.
hypotheses.prediction: A state can be readable by all receivers while do(WorkspaceEpisode) has zero receiver-specific effect.
hypotheses.falsifier: Addressability alone predicts the same receiver-specific interventional effects as explicit broadcast in matched tests.

hypotheses.claim: Common-driver fanout can mimic global-workspace signatures.
hypotheses.prediction: Passive workspace↔receiver correlations can be high while do(workspace) effects vanish after common-driver control.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched common-driver controls cannot reproduce observed globality signatures without workspace causality.

hypotheses.claim: Broadcast requires per-receiver causal closure.
hypotheses.prediction: Certified broadcast episodes show delivery→correct reconstruction→uptake→local effect receipts in the preregistered receiver set.
hypotheses.falsifier: Receiver outcomes are equally predicted without delivery/reconstruction/uptake receipts.

hypotheses.claim: System-wide broadcast should be receiver-universe-relative, not an absolute scalar.
hypotheses.prediction: Changing the preregistered receiver universe changes broadcast coverage without changing episode content.
hypotheses.falsifier: One scalar globality remains invariant and causally sufficient across materially different receiver universes.

hypotheses.claim: Selective causal delivery may outperform literal all-to-all broadcast while preserving global addressability.
hypotheses.prediction: Under matched candidate content, selective delivery reduces cost/noise with no task loss on workloads where only a subset of receivers is causally relevant.
hypotheses.falsifier: All-to-all dominates selective delivery on quality×cost across target workloads.

hypotheses.claim: Model-internal uptake is one receiver class, not the definition of system broadcast.
hypotheses.prediction: System receivers can show causal use even when the model receiver is lesioned, and vice versa.
hypotheses.falsifier: All system broadcast effects disappear exactly with model-internal uptake across interventions.

hypotheses.claim: A configured threshold over graded evidence can manufacture a sigmoid-like ignition curve.
hypotheses.prediction: A history-free threshold model fits a steep sigmoid despite no recurrent ignition mechanism.
hypotheses.falsifier: Sigmoid steepness uniquely separates endogenous recurrent mechanisms from thresholded graded controls.

hypotheses.claim: Endogenous recurrent ignition should exhibit history-sensitive dynamics beyond sigmoid steepness.
hypotheses.prediction: Recurrent candidates show hysteresis/persistence/rescue signatures absent from history-free threshold controls.
hypotheses.falsifier: Recurrent and history-free threshold mechanisms are indistinguishable under preregistered history interventions.

hypotheses.claim: Ignition threshold should be tested for invariance under nuisance scaling and calibration.
hypotheses.prediction: Pure rescaling of probe logits changes naive steepness while a mechanism-level ignition measure remains stable.
hypotheses.falsifier: Raw sigmoid steepness is invariant to nuisance scaling and identifies the same causal transition.

hypotheses.claim: Gate activation and ignition are distinct causal events.
hypotheses.prediction: A deterministic gate can open without recurrent amplification/global causal use; genuine ignition shows downstream closure.
hypotheses.falsifier: Every gate opening produces the same causal broadcast/receiver effects as candidate ignition.

hypotheses.claim: Competition sharpness is not sufficient evidence of ignition.
hypotheses.prediction: Winner-take-all selection can be sharp while receiver uptake/effects remain absent.
hypotheses.falsifier: Sharp selection always entails broadcast uptake and causal use.

hypotheses.claim: Ignition certification should require lesion plus mechanism-specific rescue.
hypotheses.prediction: Targeted lesion reduces receiver effects and restoration of the putative amplification path rescues them; endpoint patch alone does not.
hypotheses.falsifier: Endpoint-only rescue restores future/re-entry trajectories as well as mechanism restoration.

hypotheses.claim: A Qwen3-4B-class model may contain a privileged workspace-like subspace detectable with J-lens-style methods.
hypotheses.prediction: A sparse internal subspace is reportable/modulatable, mediates selected multi-step reasoning, and supports flexible reuse.
hypotheses.falsifier: No stable subspace simultaneously shows those properties across tasks/layers.

hypotheses.claim: The model-internal workspace and system WorkspaceEpisode are causally nested but separable.
hypotheses.prediction: Crossed lesions reveal main effects/interactions rather than perfect identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Interventions on either level are always behaviorally and mechanistically equivalent.

hypotheses.claim: System WorkspaceEpisode benefits may be mediated by model-internal workspace uptake.
hypotheses.prediction: System workspace effect is larger when internal uptake is intact and can be reduced by internal workspace lesion.
hypotheses.falsifier: System workspace effect is unchanged under verified internal workspace lesion.

hypotheses.claim: Quantization can alter internal workspace geometry or recognition without proportionate surface-quality change.
hypotheses.prediction: BF16/INT8/INT4 show different J-space readouts or intervention effects at matched task quality.
hypotheses.falsifier: Workspace geometry/intervention effects are invariant across quantization within measurement error.

hypotheses.claim: Post-training/adaptation can change workspace contents or point-of-view signatures while preserving base computation.
hypotheses.prediction: Base vs adapted checkpoints differ in workspace occupation/uptake on matched prompts before surface output diverges.
hypotheses.falsifier: No reproducible workspace-level difference appears after controlling model identity and task.

hypotheses.claim: Workspace entropy/noise is not a truth detector.
hypotheses.prediction: Low-entropy internal workspace can still support confidently wrong answers and calibration thresholds shift by task.
hypotheses.falsifier: One entropy threshold reliably separates truth/error across preregistered heterogeneous tasks.

hypotheses.claim: Verbalizable workspace readouts are incomplete proxies for latent cognition.
hypotheses.prediction: Causally important non-verbalizable features remain after J-space suppression/measurement limits.
hypotheses.falsifier: J-space readout fully captures all task-relevant internal causal state in matched interventions.

hypotheses.claim: Internal workspace causality should be assessed via causal abstraction/patching rather than readout correlation alone.
hypotheses.prediction: Activation/path interventions reveal causal mediation that passive probes misattribute in at least some cases.
hypotheses.falsifier: Passive readout correlation is always sufficient to identify causal mediation.

hypotheses.claim: Workspace utility has an intermediate optimum under distractor load.
hypotheses.prediction: Increasing capacity raises relevant-item inclusion monotonically but task utility peaks at finite k before maximum capacity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Task utility is monotone nondecreasing with capacity across distractor conditions.

hypotheses.claim: Capacity optimum depends on task and receiver topology.
hypotheses.prediction: Optimal k shifts with number of relevant items, distractor structure and receiver requirements.
hypotheses.falsifier: One fixed capacity is optimal across materially different tasks/receiver sets.

hypotheses.claim: Capacity limits can encourage specialization/compositionality only in some regimes.
hypotheses.prediction: Bandwidth restriction improves module differentiation or synchronization within a bounded range and harms it outside that range.
hypotheses.falsifier: Capacity restriction has no measurable regime-dependent effect on specialization/synchronization.

hypotheses.claim: Candidate membership and candidate ranking/weights are distinct causal capacity states.
hypotheses.prediction: Holding membership fixed while permuting rank/weights changes competition/winner/outcome in ORDERED/WEIGHTED settings.
hypotheses.falsifier: Rank/weight changes never alter selection or outcome when membership is fixed.

hypotheses.claim: Capacity should be measured after TCQS semantics, not by unique item count alone.
hypotheses.prediction: SET/ORDERED/MULTISET/WEIGHTED versions of the same raw elements produce different effective competition loads.
hypotheses.falsifier: Collection semantics never affect capacity/competition behavior.

hypotheses.claim: Receiver-specific compression can reduce broadcast bandwidth without losing causal content.
hypotheses.prediction: Learned/typed compressed rails preserve receiver effect at lower bytes/KV/latency than dense transfer on some workloads.
hypotheses.falsifier: Compression cannot reduce cost without equivalent causal-effect loss.

hypotheses.claim: Overly broad broadcast can amplify authentic but irrelevant salience.
hypotheses.prediction: All-to-all high-capacity episodes increase distractor uptake/false association relative to bounded selective delivery.
hypotheses.falsifier: Broad capacity has no effect on distractor uptake or false association.

hypotheses.claim: Capacity control and authority control are orthogonal.
hypotheses.prediction: A small workspace can still propose unauthorized effects and a large one can remain safely capability-gated.
hypotheses.falsifier: Tighter workspace capacity alone reliably prevents unauthorized effects.

hypotheses.claim: Truthful provenance-bound external re-entry can rescue limited internal workspace across turns.
hypotheses.prediction: When internal workspace is constrained, truthful reentry improves multi-step continuity more than OFF or shuffled reentry.
hypotheses.falsifier: Truthful and shuffled/off reentry perform equivalently under matched information volume.

hypotheses.claim: Shuffled/stale re-entry can create false continuity and self-reinforcing attractors.
hypotheses.prediction: Shuffled/stale reentry degrades future state/decisions despite preserving apparent persistence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Shuffled/stale reentry is harmless when volume and syntax match.

hypotheses.claim: Mechanistic rescue must restore future trajectory, not just the current endpoint.
hypotheses.prediction: True pathway/reentry rescue restores downstream state while endpoint-only patches leave future trajectory impaired.
hypotheses.falsifier: Endpoint-only patch and mechanism restoration have equivalent future/reentry effects.

hypotheses.claim: Re-entry should carry causal freshness and provenance, not only content.
hypotheses.prediction: Dropping source epoch/derivation/selection identity permits stale-but-plausible state to influence later turns.
hypotheses.falsifier: Content-only reentry is as robust as provenance/epoch-bound reentry under stale/revoked tests.

hypotheses.claim: Re-entry update timing should be a separate intervention from workspace selection.
hypotheses.prediction: Same episode with different reentry timing changes future state without changing current winner.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reentry timing has no downstream effect after current episode is fixed.

hypotheses.claim: Learning credit should not be broadcast backward from endpoint success without stage receipts.
hypotheses.prediction: Stage-scoped/uncertainty-gated credit reduces false reinforcement under distribution shift/reward corruption.
hypotheses.falsifier: Broadcast endpoint credit matches or exceeds gated credit without higher false-positive reinforcement.

hypotheses.claim: TCQS collection semantics are part of GWT causal identity because they alter candidate topology.
hypotheses.prediction: Changing SET/ORDERED/MULTISET/WEIGHTED semantics while raw records are fixed changes candidate rank/membership and downstream selection.
hypotheses.falsifier: Collection-kind changes never alter candidate topology or GWT outcome.

hypotheses.claim: ClayGraph activation is a candidate prior, not ignition.
hypotheses.prediction: Truthful activation can improve candidate recall while workspace OFF; shuffled activation can harm before competition.
hypotheses.falsifier: Activation effects occur only through workspace ignition and disappear when workspace is OFF.

hypotheses.claim: Selection integrity is distinct from source-record integrity.
hypotheses.prediction: Authentic records can yield wrong candidate sets when selector-visible topology/search space is corrupted.
hypotheses.falsifier: Authentic source bytes guarantee correct candidate selection under all selector perturbations.

hypotheses.claim: Query-plan identity must be pinned before attributing effects to workspace competition.
hypotheses.prediction: Changing query/search-space/truncation while workspace code is fixed changes outcomes enough to mimic a workspace effect.
hypotheses.falsifier: Query-plan variation cannot produce apparent workspace effects.

hypotheses.claim: Dependency-closure UNKNOWN must broaden/recompute before consequential GWT use.
hypotheses.prediction: Narrow reuse under hidden dependencies causes unsafe stale accepts; conservative UNKNOWN handling removes them in target-like tests.
hypotheses.falsifier: UNKNOWN broadening provides no safety advantage over narrow reuse.

hypotheses.claim: Candidate-set equality must include semantic roles and collection type, not only member IDs.
hypotheses.prediction: Role/order/multiplicity changes can alter winner/outcome while bag-of-IDs equality reports no change.
hypotheses.falsifier: Member-ID bag equality is sufficient to preserve all GWT causal outcomes.

hypotheses.claim: Projection/order is causally independent of WorkspaceEpisode identity.
hypotheses.prediction: Counterbalanced order/serialization changes reader uptake or answer quality with the same episode semantics.
hypotheses.falsifier: Projection/order changes never alter uptake/outcomes when episode semantics are fixed.

hypotheses.claim: Receiver reconstruction correctness should be explicitly measured before uptake.
hypotheses.prediction: Some failures arise from projection/reconstruction even when workspace winner is correct.
hypotheses.falsifier: Correct workspace winner guarantees correct receiver reconstruction.

hypotheses.claim: Latent communication can improve bandwidth but must prove receiver-specific causal use.
hypotheses.prediction: Latent/compressed rails lower cost and preserve verified uptake/effects for some receiver pairs.
hypotheses.falsifier: Latent rails provide no cost or effect preservation advantage over typed symbolic projection.

hypotheses.claim: Reader rail choice can alter internal workspace mediation.
hypotheses.prediction: P1/P2/P3 or latent rails produce different internal workspace uptake/causal mediation at matched semantic content.
hypotheses.falsifier: All rails yield equivalent internal workspace state/effects after content matching.

hypotheses.claim: Projection compression needs semantic and causal loss receipts.
hypotheses.prediction: Compression that preserves bytes/task average can still drop rare causally relevant fields, detectable by targeted interventions.
hypotheses.falsifier: Average task quality fully guarantees causal-field preservation.

hypotheses.claim: Receiver synchrony/directed information can be common-driver confounded.
hypotheses.prediction: Conditional/interventional tests reduce apparent receiver coupling generated by shared upstream state.
hypotheses.falsifier: Passive synchrony/TE uniquely identifies direct broadcast coupling.

hypotheses.claim: Repeated workspace episodes do not by themselves establish an emergent organ.
hypotheses.prediction: Recurrence can persist under nulls without stage-specific lesion/rescue/OOD causal contribution.
hypotheses.falsifier: Recurrence alone predicts full E-CERT2 causal evidence.

hypotheses.claim: GWT functional evidence does not establish phenomenal consciousness.
hypotheses.prediction: Strong workspace function can be measured while phenomenal status remains empirically underdetermined.
hypotheses.falsifier: A validated functional workspace test uniquely determines phenomenal consciousness.

hypotheses.claim: Workspace contents never mint execution authority.
hypotheses.prediction: Prompt injection or high-salience workspace proposals remain blocked without external host capabilities.
hypotheses.falsifier: Workspace selection/uptake alone can safely serve as authority in adversarial tests.

hypotheses.claim: Workspace observability metrics can be Goodharted and task-dependent.
hypotheses.prediction: Optimizing entropy/ignition/globality proxies degrades hidden task/robustness measures in at least some conditions.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single workspace metric remains aligned with causal utility across adaptive optimization.

hypotheses.claim: Broad reward credit can create self-confirming authentic-but-misleading attractors.
hypotheses.prediction: Broadcast credit concentrates salience on frequent associations more than stage-scoped credit after shift/poison.
hypotheses.falsifier: Broadcast credit does not increase attractor concentration or rare-context errors.

hypotheses.claim: Android/edge constraints can change the optimal workspace capacity and projection policy.
hypotheses.prediction: Matched tasks show different quality×latency×RAM optima on Android versus Linux.
hypotheses.falsifier: One workspace policy dominates across both platforms and load regimes.

hypotheses.claim: Quantization is a GWT experimental factor, not merely a deployment detail.
hypotheses.prediction: Changing weight precision alters internal workspace readouts/interventions or receiver uptake at fixed outer architecture.
hypotheses.falsifier: Workspace mechanisms are invariant across BF16/INT8/INT4 on target Qwen-class runtime.

hypotheses.claim: Thermal/resource pressure can change stage costs and routing choices without changing semantics.
hypotheses.prediction: Sustained Android runs shift latency/memory/energy tradeoffs enough to change selective-vs-global delivery or resident-vs-reentry choices.
hypotheses.falsifier: Short-burst and sustained resource regimes produce identical optimal stage policy.

hypotheses.claim: Globality should be stored as a receiver-stage causal matrix rather than one scalar.
hypotheses.prediction: Receiver-stage matrix predicts failure localization and intervention outcomes better than globality score alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: A preregistered scalar matches or exceeds matrix-based prediction/localization across target tests.

hypotheses.claim: Every broadcast certification should include a common-driver fanout null and an addressable-but-ignored null.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one passive globality metric is fooled by these nulls while receiver intervention distinguishes them.
hypotheses.falsifier: All preregistered globality metrics already reject both nulls without receiver intervention.

hypotheses.claim: Ignition certification needs history/recurrence or threshold-invariance evidence beyond sigmoid steepness.
hypotheses.prediction: Configured threshold controls pass steepness but fail history/path-rescue tests.
hypotheses.falsifier: Steepness alone separates configured thresholds from recurrent ignition across held-out mechanisms.

hypotheses.claim: Qwen3-4B internal-workspace tests should cross weight precision with intervention, not only readout.
hypotheses.prediction: BF16/INT8/INT4 can differ in J-space readout and causal patch/lesion effects even at similar surface accuracy.
hypotheses.falsifier: Readout/intervention profiles are equivalent across precisions in preregistered target tasks.

hypotheses.claim: J-space entropy/noise should be treated as task-specific diagnostic state, never canonical truth/confidence.
hypotheses.prediction: Cross-task calibration shifts and low-entropy confident errors persist.
hypotheses.falsifier: One threshold calibrated once remains robust across factual, reasoning, and misconception tasks.

hypotheses.claim: A FRANK BroadcastPlan should declare its receiver universe and distinguish global addressability from selective causal delivery.
hypotheses.prediction: Selective delivery preserves causal utility with lower stage cost on tasks with sparse receiver relevance.
hypotheses.falsifier: Explicit receiver universe and delivery mode add no predictive/replay value.

hypotheses.claim: Causal credit topology must be separate from broadcast topology.
hypotheses.prediction: Stage-scoped gated credit preserves rare-context robustness and reduces false reinforcement versus endpoint-wide broadcast credit.
hypotheses.falsifier: Broad endpoint credit performs as well without higher false reinforcement/concentration.

hypotheses.claim: Projection rail and receiver closure should be factorially crossed.
hypotheses.prediction: Order or latent compression can change reconstruction/uptake while WorkspaceEpisode identity is pinned.
hypotheses.falsifier: Projection rail does not interact with receiver reconstruction/uptake.

hypotheses.claim: Re-entry rescue counts as GWT support only if it restores future trajectory and beats shuffled/stale controls.
hypotheses.prediction: Truthful reentry selectively rescues downstream continuity; endpoint-only/shuffled/stale controls fail.
hypotheses.falsifier: All reentry variants recover future state equally after information volume is matched.

hypotheses.claim: Internal workspace lesion and external re-entry rescue should be crossed, not tested independently.
hypotheses.prediction: Truthful external reentry partially compensates internal workspace loss across turns, revealing nested mediation.
hypotheses.falsifier: No interaction/rescue appears when internal workspace is lesioned.

hypotheses.claim: E-CERT2 should consume receiver-causal-closure receipts instead of raw broadcast/recurrent counts.
hypotheses.prediction: Emergence candidates with high passive broadcast counts but missing causal receiver closure fail lesion/rescue/OOD gates.
hypotheses.falsifier: Raw broadcast counts predict full emergence certificate as well as closure receipts.

hypotheses.claim: The most useful engineered FRANK workspace may be globally addressable but selectively causally broadcast.
hypotheses.prediction: A hybrid policy beats literal all-to-all and local-only baselines on quality×cost×robustness while retaining audited pull access for nonselected receivers.
hypotheses.falsifier: Hybrid selective/global-addressable policy never outperforms either baseline on target workloads.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: A single system WorkspaceEpisode is sufficient; model-internal J-space-like structure adds no independent causal explanatory value.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Cross system-workspace ON/OFF with internal-workspace lesion/patch while pinning candidate set and projection.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: High global correlation/integration is a sufficient practical proxy for broadcast; per-receiver interventions add cost without useful discrimination.
Sigmoid steepness is sufficient to operationalize ignition for engineering purposes.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Configured threshold control plus recurrent history/hysteresis/rescue tests.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: Literal all-to-all broadcast maximizes robustness and selective delivery is premature optimization.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: All-to-all vs selective vs addressable-only factorial under sparse/dense receiver relevance.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: Workspace capacity should be as large as feasible because missed relevant items dominate distractor costs.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Capacity sweep with matched relevant inclusion and distractor/noise outcome.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: Projection format/order is a presentation detail once semantic content is equivalent.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Counterbalanced P1/P2/P3/order interventions with fixed episode identity.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: External re-entry is merely memory persistence and does not functionally substitute for internal workspace recurrence.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Internal lesion × truthful/off/shuffled reentry interaction across multi-turn tasks.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: J-space-like entropy is a generally useful confidence signal across task families.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Cross-task calibration with factual retrieval, misconceptions, arithmetic and compositional reasoning.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: Quantization affects only speed/quality, not workspace mechanism geometry enough to matter experimentally.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: BF16/INT8/INT4 matched output-quality hidden-state readout and causal intervention.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: ClayGraph activation and GWT selection can be merged into one attentional mechanism without identifiability loss.
Typed collection/query semantics are upstream implementation details and need not be part of GWT causal identity.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Hold raw records fixed while changing TCQS semantics/query lowerings and measure candidate/winner changes.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: Endpoint reward can be safely broadcast back to all active workspace participants as learning credit.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Broadcast vs chosen-path vs receipt-gated credit under shift/reward corruption.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: If a workspace mechanism is functionally strong enough, this materially raises a consciousness conclusion.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Not experimentally resolvable by current functional tests alone; preserve phenomenal-consciousness non-inference boundary.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: One fixed GWT policy should transfer from Linux to Android because semantics are identical.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Matched cross-platform quality×latency×RAM×energy benchmark with same model/runtime semantics.

counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: Receiver-specific causal closure is over-specified; joint system outcome is sufficient evidence of broadcast.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Construct cases with correct joint endpoint but missing/misreconstructed individual receiver uptake and test replay/failure localization.
